title: Degree-zero Picard point injectivity and torsion lifting under field extension
statement: Let $k\subseteq k'$ be algebraically closed fields [def-sc-field-extension], and let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a proper smooth connected curve [def-sc-curves]. Write $X'=X\times_k k'$ and $f':X'\to\operatorname{Spec}k'$ [def-pc-base-change]. Let $G\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ and $G'\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}(X')$ be subgroups whose underlying sets are the degree-zero Picard classes [def-sc-pic0]. Let $j:G\to G'$ be a homomorphism whose underlying Picard classes are the canonical pullbacks. For a natural number $n$ nonzero in $k$, $j$ is injective and every $y\in G'$ with $y^n=1$ is $j(x)$ for some $x\in G$ with $x^n=1$.

source.place: Proper-case Kummer naturality sentence and affine-case Picard-torsion paragraph

proof.text: Smooth connected curves over an algebraically closed field are geometrically integral and smooth of relative dimension one: regularity and geometric connectedness give geometric irreducibility, and smoothness gives geometric reducedness. Use Jacobian representability to identify the degree-zero subgroup with rational points of its abelian variety, respecting multiplication. Apply the same identification after extension; base change of curves supplies its connectedness and dimension.

The Jacobian base-change compatibility square, evaluated on Spec kprime, identifies the stipulated Picard pullback j with extension of rational points of the original Jacobian. The equalities specifying G and Gprime transport between subgroup models of Pic-zero. This identification respects multiplication by the representing group-law compatibility.

Extension is injective on rational points. A Spec k point is determined by its image x and its map from the residue field at x to k. Equality after Spec kprime gives the same image x and equal residue maps after composition with k -> kprime. Since the latter field embedding is injective, the original residue maps agree. Thus the original scheme points agree (the existing Scheme.SpecMap_comp_injective formalizes this argument). Restriction to the representing degree-zero groups yields injectivity of j.

Nonzero n in k implies n > 0 and the characteristic does not divide n. Clause (c) of the abelian-variety estimate says rational points of the finite etale torsion subgroup scheme J[n] are unchanged by extension. A point y of Gprime with y^n=1 corresponds to a kprime-point of J[n], since the kernel of the multiplication morphism represents precisely these points. Lift that point to a k-point of J[n] and map it to J(k); it has nth power one and extends to the point representing y. Transport back along the group equivalence to obtain x in G, x^n=1 and j(x)=y.

proof_origin.place: Proper degree-one Jacobian comparison and affine correction; canonical point-map identification and residue-field injectivity expanded by S1.

theorem picZero_torsion_base_change
    {k k' : Type u} [Field k] [Field k'] [IsAlgClosed k] [IsAlgClosed k'] [Algebra k k']
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsConnectedCurve f] [Smooth f] [IsProper f]
    (G : Subgroup X.Pic) (hG : (G : Set X.Pic) = f.picZero)
    (G' : Subgroup (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k')))).Pic)
    (hG' : (G' : Set (pullback f
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k')))).Pic) =
      (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k')))).picZero)
    (j : G →* G')
    (hj : ∀ L : G, (j L).val = Scheme.Pic.mapHom
      (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k')))) L.val)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : (n : k) ≠ 0) :
    Function.Injective j ∧ ∀ y : G', y ^ n = 1 → ∃ x : G, x ^ n = 1 ∧ j x = y
